rationale: This is a cosmetic time-series wrapper (TS_MAX over 3 periods) on the already-tested "Maturity Funding Gap," replicating exactly the persistence transform the archive already applied to the fixed-claim buffer (where it yielded essentially no improvement), so little new economic content is being tested.

This is the fifth R&D-rank-gated variant in the archive and simply multiplies the already-strong standalone "Fixed-Claim Cash Buffer" by an R&D weight, a recombination that historically attenuates the strong leg rather than isolating a distinct crowding-out mechanism, and any result will be hard to attribute to the interaction.
This is "Accrual-Heavy Equity Recycling" with the accrual leg rescaled from assets to |ib|+|oancf| — a denominator change only, i.e., a direct cosmetic rediscovery of an already-evaluated signal.

A triple product of two already-archived R&D interactions ("Innovation Financing Horizon" and "Innovation Per-Share Conversion") adds a third conditioning dimension that thins the effective sample and makes attribution impossible, without any new mechanism beyond the two components already tested.

The point about avoiding mechanical overlap between the payout leg and the coverage leg is a legitimate construction improvement, but the signal still sits squarely between the archive's "Cash-Covered Total Payout," "Cash-Quality Repurchase," and "Post-Interest Payout Coverage," making it an incremental fourth payout-coverage variant rather than a substantively different idea.

The construction is internally consistent (a nonnegative rank weight preserving the signed growth term) and is motivated by a diagnosed FMB/alpha divergence in "Gross-Profit Per-Share Growth," though it is close to the well-known accruals-quality-times-profitability family (e.g., cash-based operating profitability) and the monotone weight risks the result being driven entirely by the growth leg.
